In contrast, Australia had a near-perfect game. Their bowlers, led by Megan Schutt's five-wicket haul, set up the victory with a stellar display in the first innings. The batting duo of Georgia Voll and Phoebe Litchfield also impressed, making light work of the target. As the teams face off in the second ODI, India will be desperate to bounce back and level the series. Can they address their batting concerns and put up a stronger challenge against the formidable Australian side? We shall find out soon. Stay tuned for toss and team updates in a while.

India's batting concerns are glaring, with the team folding inside 35 overs. The scoring rate was also a worry, with the batters struggling to accelerate. Smriti Mandhana's form is a particular concern, as she has failed to live up to expectations. While a few batters got starts, they couldn't convert them into substantial innings.

Hello and welcome to one and all. India Women takes on Australia Women in the 2nd ODI of this 3-match ODI series. The Australian women's team is riding high after a dominant display in the first ODI, taking a 1-0 lead in the series. The hosts comprehensively outplayed India, dismissing them for a paltry total and then chasing it down with ease.

We are now set for the second ODI of the three-match series between Australia Women and India Women. After suffering a crushing defeat at the Allan Border Field in Brisbane, the Women in Blue face a quick turnaround at the same venue to keep the series alive. The series opener was a one-sided affair, with Australia’s bowlers dismantling India for a mere 100 runs. The hosts made light work of the chase, reaching the target in just 16.2 overs. Despite the dismal outing, India can take some solace in managing to claim five wickets, with Renuka Singh Thakur and leg-spinner Priya Mishra among the wicket-takers. Newcomers Saima Thakor and Titas Sadhu, still early in their ODI careers, will need to step up with the ball in this crucial encounter. The primary concern for India is their underwhelming batting performance. In the absence of Shafali Verma, Smriti Mandhana will need to lead from the front and set the tone at the top of the order. Skipper Harmanpreet Kaur, Jemimah Rodrigues, and Richa Ghosh must rise to the occasion if the visitors are to push the series to a decider. On the other hand, Australia were clinical in every department in the first match, giving their opponents no breathing room with the ball or in the field. Megan Schutt led the charge with a superb maiden five-wicket haul, while the rest of the bowling unit chipped in seamlessly in a collective display of excellence. Although they would have hoped to be more convincing in the chase, debutant Georgia Voll’s composed knock to guide them home was the highlight for the hosts. India have never won a bilateral ODI series against Australia in women’s cricket, and keeping that dream alive will demand nothing short of an exceptional all-round performance. With their backs against the wall, can Harmanpreet Kaur and Co. rise to the challenge and force a decider? Or will Tahlia McGrath’s confident and well-drilled Australian unit prove too strong for the tourists yet again? We shall find out together.
